meta.title: Roma migrations · South Asia to the global diaspora
meta.description: Seven-phase supplied reconstruction, with 28 wave rows retained, Roma/Sinti primary and Dom/Lom comparative. Modern net-mobile weights are not a census of present-day Roma. Default 1 dot = 1,000 people. Source low/central/high values are visualization scenarios, not censuses or statistical confidence intervals. Unknown archival headcounts stay null. Genetic effective size and ancestry percentages are not converted into added people. Dated descendant-support priors are disclosed bookkeeping assumptions, not observed births or local admixture.

evidenceCodes.REPORT: User-supplied synthesis, unreviewed except specifically linked preparation corrections

visualizationExtensions.basis: Prepared field-presence extension, separate from research.original and the28 supplied source rows.

residentReconstruction.basis: Separate geographic resident reconstruction. Dated institutional estimates, chiefly CoE2012 and later reproductions, are chosen as2012/2025 display references rather than asserted as2025 censuses. Country groups are disjoint; existing locally remaining child stocks are included once, and only the target deficit is added. Historical mobile groups do not classify every modern resident. Ukraine displacement and differing umbrella/census categories remain unresolved. No original source population, ancestry or historical chronology is overwritten.

continuityReconstruction.basis: User-directed continuity reconstruction: separately identified South Asian comparative origins visibly pass through Iran and Anatolia before the southward Syrian/Iraqi distribution. This display sequence is not established by the Sasanian traditions or the reported seventh-century lower-Tigris-to-Syria transfer. Those original directions, textual dates and hypotheses remain unchanged in the source register. The staged display intervals and long cohort transits are explicit visualization choices, not observed personal travel times.
continuityReconstruction.sourceW03Direction: Lower Tigris to northern Syria; late-seventh-century reported forced transfer, retained as original evidence rather than asserted as proof of the changed user-directed display route.
continuityReconstruction.support: Every addition is progressive, descendantSupport:true, and requires an existing surviving incoming lineage. Initial origins are visible in South Asia at200; no foreign pool is seeded independently.
